learningObjectives.title: The sales process and customer service

questions.q: Which production method is used to make a single, unique, one-off product to a customer's specific requirements?
options: Job production
Batch production
Flow production
Lean production
questions.explain: Job production makes one-off, individual items such as a tailored suit or a bespoke wedding cake.

questions.q: Flow production is best described as:
options: Producing large quantities of identical products continuously on a production line
Making a single unique product for one customer
Making small groups of identical products in stages
Producing goods only once individual orders are received
questions.explain: Flow (mass) production runs continuously to make large volumes of standardised, identical products.

questions.q: A bakery makes 200 identical loaves, then changes the line over to make 200 identical bread rolls. Which production method is this?
options: Batch production
Job production
Flow production
Cell production
questions.explain: Producing groups of identical items one batch at a time before switching output is batch production.

questions.q: Quality control is best defined as:
options: Inspecting and checking products at the end of the production process
Making every employee responsible for quality at each stage
Setting national industry quality standards
Training suppliers to prevent all faults
questions.explain: Quality control relies on inspecting finished output to identify and remove faulty products.

questions.q: How does quality assurance mainly differ from quality control?
options: Quality assurance checks quality throughout the whole process, not just at the end
Quality assurance only inspects finished goods
Quality assurance ignores customer requirements
Quality assurance removes the need for any staff involvement
questions.explain: Quality assurance builds quality in at every stage to prevent faults, rather than only inspecting the finished product.

questions.q: E-commerce refers to:
options: Buying and selling goods and services over the internet
Selling goods only in physical high-street shops
Selling goods by post through a catalogue
Selling only to other businesses
questions.explain: E-commerce is trading goods and services electronically, typically through websites.

questions.q: Which is a likely benefit to a business of providing good customer service?
options: Increased customer loyalty and repeat purchases
Higher variable costs of production
A fall in the business's brand reputation
Reduced sales revenue over time
questions.explain: Good customer service builds loyalty, encouraging customers to return and recommend the business.

questions.q: M-commerce specifically refers to buying and selling using:
options: Mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets
Physical shops on the high street
Printed mail-order catalogues
Telephone landlines only
questions.explain: M-commerce is a form of e-commerce carried out through mobile devices like smartphones and tablets.

questions.q: Why is good product knowledge important for sales staff?
options: It helps them answer customer questions and recommend suitable products
It reduces the amount of stock the business must hold
It automatically lowers the business's fixed costs
It removes any need for the business to advertise
questions.explain: Well-informed staff can advise customers accurately, improving satisfaction and boosting sales.

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal source of finance?
options: Retained profit
Bank loan
Bank overdraft
Trade credit
questions.explain: Retained profit is generated within the business, making it an internal source of finance.

questions.q: An overdraft is best described as a:
options: Short-term source of finance allowing a business to spend more than is in its account
Long-term loan repaid over many years
Sale of new shares to investors
Government grant that does not need repaying
questions.explain: An overdraft lets a business withdraw more than its balance for short-term cash flow needs.

questions.q: Trade credit provides finance to a business by:
options: Allowing it to buy goods now and pay the supplier later
Selling shares to new investors
Borrowing a fixed sum from a bank
Using the owner's own savings
questions.explain: Trade credit delays payment to suppliers, easing short-term cash flow.

questions.q: A firm has fixed costs of £12,000, a selling price of £8 per unit and variable costs of £4 per unit. What is its break-even output?
options: 3,000 units
1,500 units
6,000 units
2,000 units
questions.explain: Break-even = fixed costs / (price − variable cost) = 12,000 / (8 − 4) = 3,000 units.

questions.q: A business has sales revenue of £80,000 and total costs of £55,000. What is its profit?
questions.explain: Profit = revenue − total costs = 80,000 − 55,000 = £25,000.

questions.q: Crowdfunding raises finance by:
options: Collecting small amounts of money from a large number of people, usually online
Borrowing a single large sum from one bank
Selling off the business's fixed assets
Using an overdraft facility
questions.explain: Crowdfunding pools small contributions from many people, typically via an online platform.

questions.q: What is a likely effect on businesses if interest rates rise?
options: The cost of borrowing increases, which may reduce investment and spending
Borrowing immediately becomes cheaper for firms
Exports automatically increase for all firms
Inflation is guaranteed to fall to zero
questions.explain: Higher interest rates raise loan repayment costs and tend to reduce borrowing and consumer demand.

questions.q: If the value of the pound rises against other currencies, UK exports generally become:
options: More expensive for foreign buyers
Cheaper for foreign buyers
Free of any charge abroad
Completely unaffected
questions.explain: A stronger pound means overseas customers pay more in their currency, making exports dearer.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a business behaving ethically?
options: Paying suppliers a fair price and treating workers fairly
Using child labour to reduce costs
Dumping waste illegally to save money
Deliberately misleading customers in adverts
questions.explain: Ethical behaviour means acting morally, such as fair treatment of workers and suppliers.

questions.q: A business has a large variable-rate bank loan. If interest rates rise, the most likely immediate effect is that:
options: Its loan repayment costs will increase
Its loan will automatically be cancelled
Its sales revenue will automatically rise
Its fixed costs will fall to zero
questions.explain: On a variable-rate loan, higher interest rates directly increase the interest the business must pay.

questions.q: A shop sells a customer a kettle that is faulty and not of satisfactory quality. Under UK consumer law, the customer is most likely entitled to:
options: A repair, replacement or refund
Nothing, as all sales are final
Only store credit after one year
A discount on future purchases only
questions.explain: Consumer law requires goods to be of satisfactory quality, entitling buyers of faulty goods to a repair, replacement or refund.
